title: The island motel
logline: Wednesday. A motel on the island, $190 a night, which is twenty-six nights of the Driftwood. Wood sits on the bed and does the arithmetic aloud to the sketchbook, since the dog's not here.

panels.composition: A clean island motel room, white linens, a window onto madrones. WOOD on the bed's edge in the chore coat, the suit on the door. The sketchbook on his knee.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, a bright clean motel room with white linens and a window onto madrone trees, a thin man in a canvas chore coat sitting on the bed's edge with a sketchbook, a suit hanging on the door

panels.composition: The receipt: $190.00. Beside it, in the sketchbook, his arithmetic: 190 ÷ 7.25 = 26.2 nights of the Driftwood.

image.prompt: razor-sharp brush and ink with pristine architectural perspective, blinding clear summer light in soft cerulean and pale linen watercolor, close-up of a motel receipt beside a sketchbook page with a short handwritten division sum
image.notes: Letter after: $190.00 · '26 nights of the Driftwood.'

panels.composition: Wood, to the sketchbook, because there's no dog.

balloons.text: Twenty-six nights. At the desk. To sleep one night here.
...You're not going to say anything either.

panels.composition: The empty half of the bed. Where the dog would be, in the garage. A hand, flat, on the linen.
